questions.text: What command can a technician use on a computer to see if DNS is functioning properly?
options: ipconfig
net share
nslookup
net use
questions.explanation: nslookup sends a query straight to a DNS server and shows the answer, so it directly tests name resolution. ipconfig only shows which DNS server is configured; net share and net use deal with file shares.

questions.text: Which two OSI model layers have the same functionality as two layers of the TCP/IP model? (Choose two.)
options: physical
data link
network
transport
session
questions.explanation: OSI transport maps one-to-one onto TCP/IP transport, and OSI network onto the TCP/IP internet layer. OSI physical and data link are merged into TCP/IP's single network access layer, and session/presentation are folded into TCP/IP's application layer.

questions.text: What is one advantage of using the cut-through switching method instead of the store-and-forward switching method?
options: provides the flexibility to support any of Ethernet speeds
has a lower latency appropriate for high-performance computing applications
makes a fast forwarding decision based on the source MAC address of the frame
has a positive impact on bandwidth by dropping most of the invalid frames
questions.explanation: Cut-through starts forwarding as soon as it has read the destination MAC, which gives lower latency. The trade-off is that it can't check the FCS first, so it lets more invalid frames through — dropping bad frames is store-and-forward's strength.

questions.text: Which solution improves web response time by deploying multiple web servers and DNS servers?
options: memcaching
distributed databases
sharding
load balancing
questions.explanation: Load balancing puts several web and DNS servers behind the service so requests are answered in parallel. Memcaching keeps hot data in memory, sharding splits one database across servers, and distributed databases speed up database access.

questions.text: What will a host on an Ethernet network do if it receives a frame with a unicast destination MAC address that does not match its own MAC address?
options: It will remove the frame from the media.
It will forward the frame to the next host.
It will strip off the data-link frame to check the destination IP address.
It will discard the frame.
questions.explanation: Every NIC compares a frame's destination MAC with its own. If they don't match (and it isn't broadcast or a multicast group it joined), the frame is discarded and never passed up to the network layer.

questions.text: What is the common term given to SNMP log messages that are generated by network devices and sent to the SNMP server?
options: auditing
warnings
acknowledgments
traps
questions.explanation: SNMP traps are unsolicited messages an agent sends to the manager when something happens, ranging from simple status updates to urgent alerts.

questions.text: What is the function of the Nslookup utility?
options: to manually force a client to send a DHCP request
to display all cached DNS entries on a host
to view the network settings on a host
to manually query the name servers to resolve a given host name
questions.explanation: nslookup manually queries DNS servers to resolve a name. Viewing cached entries is ipconfig /displaydns, and forcing a DHCP request is ipconfig /renew.

an address that reaches every host inside a local subnet
an address that reaches a specific group of hosts
an address that reaches one specific host
questions.explanation: MAC addresses beginning 01-00-5E are IPv4 multicast MACs, which reach the group of hosts that joined that multicast group. Broadcast would be FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF.

questions.text: Refer to the exhibit. The PC is sending a packet to the Server on the remote network. Router R1 is performing NAT overload. From the perspective of the PC, match the NAT address type with the correct IP address. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: Inside local is the PC's own private address, 10.130.5.76. With NAT overload, R1 translates it to its own outside interface address, so the inside global is 192.0.2.1. The outside global is simply the server's real address, 203.0.113.5. The router interfaces 10.130.5.1, 192.0.2.2 and 203.0.113.14 aren't any of these.

questions.text: Match the OSI layer to the layer number. (Not all options are used.)
questions.explanation: From the bottom up, the OSI model is: 1 physical, 2 data link, 3 network, 4 transport, 5 session, 6 presentation, 7 application. "Internet layer" and "network access layer" are TCP/IP model names and have no OSI number.

questions.text: A high school in New York (school A) is using videoconferencing technology to establish student interactions with another high school (school B) in Russia. The videoconferencing is conducted between two end devices through the Internet. The network administrator of school A configures the end device with the IP address 209.165.201.10. The administrator sends a request for the IP address for the end device in school B and the response is 192.168.25.10. Neither school is using a VPN. The administrator knows immediately that this IP will not work. Why?
options: This is a link-local address.
This is a private IP address.
There is an IP address conflict.
This is a loopback address.
questions.explanation: 192.168.0.0/16 is private (RFC 1918) address space, which isn't routed on the Internet. School B's device would need NAT (or a VPN) to be reachable. Link-local is 169.254.x.x and loopback is 127.x.x.x.

questions.text: Refer to the exhibit. An organization is using static NAT to translate the private IP address of Host A to a single public IP address leased from the ISP. Which address is the inside global address of Host A?
questions.explanation: The inside global address is how Host A appears to the outside world: the NAT router's public address, 209.165.202.129. 192.168.1.10 is Host A's inside local address, and 203.0.113.2 belongs to the HQ side.

questions.text: Consider the following routing table entry for R1. What is the significance of the Serial0/0/0?
options: It is the interface on the final destination router that is directly connected to the 10.1.1.0/24 network.
It is the R1 interface through which the EIGRP update was learned.
It is the interface on the next-hop router when the destination IP address the 10.1.1.0/24 network.
It is the interface on R1 used to send data that is destined for 10.1.1.0/24.
questions.explanation: The interface at the end of a route entry is R1's own exit interface for that destination. 209.165.200.226 is the next-hop address, D marks an EIGRP route, and [90/2170112] is the administrative distance and metric.

questions.text: A device has an IPv6 address listed as 2001:0DB8:75a3:0214:0607:1234:aa10:ba01. What is the interface ID of the device?
options: ba01
questions.explanation: With the usual /64 split, the first four hextets are the prefix (routing prefix plus subnet ID) and the last four, 0607:1234:aa10:ba01, are the 64-bit interface ID.

questions.text: In what two situations would UDP be the preferred transport protocol over TCP? (Choose two.)
options: when applications need to guarantee that a packet arrives intact, in sequence, and unduplicated
when a faster delivery mechanism is needed
when delivery overhead is not an issue
when applications do not need to guarantee delivery of the data
when destination port numbers are dynamic
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless and best-effort: no handshake, acknowledgements or sequencing, which makes it fast and low-overhead. It suits traffic like voice and video, where delivery doesn't have to be guaranteed. Guaranteed, in-order delivery is TCP's job.

questions.text: Refer to the exhibit. A computer that is configured with the IPv4 address as shown in the exhibit is unable to access the internet. What is the problem?
questions.context:
IP address:       192.168.44.150
Subnet mask:      255.255.255.224
Default gateway:  192.168.44.161
Preferred DNS:    64.102.255.44
Alternate DNS:    128.107.241.185
options: The gateway address is in the wrong subnet.
The IP address is a network address.
The settings were not validated.
The IP address is a broadcast address.
questions.explanation: A /27 mask (255.255.255.224) makes blocks of 32. .150 falls in 192.168.44.128/27 (hosts .129–.158, broadcast .159), but the gateway .161 belongs to the next block, .160/27, so the PC can't reach it. .150 is neither the network nor the broadcast address.

questions.text: Match the Layer 2 frame field names to the correctly ordered locations for an Ethernet frame. Fields should be ordered from the beginning of the Ethernet frame to the end.
questions.explanation: An Ethernet frame runs: Preamble → Start Frame Delimiter → Destination MAC → Source MAC → EtherType → Data → FCS. The destination comes before the source so a switch can start its forwarding decision as early as possible.

questions.text: What IPv4-related DNS record type is used by a DNS server in response to a host requesting for a web server address via the URL?
options: AAAA record
NS record
A record
MX record
questions.explanation: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address. AAAA is the IPv6 equivalent, MX points to mail servers, and NS names the authoritative name servers.
